content: 1. Prolongation of the QTc interval is a potential risk. Avoid using the drug or consider an alternative. If concomitant use is unavoidable, obtain baseline and follow-up ECGs and electrolyte levels before and after initiating any drug known to prolong the QTc interval. Continue periodic monitoring as clinically indicated during treatment. 2. Erythromycin base and insulin degludec may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Both drugs lower blood glucose levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Erythromycin base and insulin aspart may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Both drugs lower blood glucose levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin base and inhaled insulin may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Both drugs lower blood glucose levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of irinotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious; use an alternative drug. 6. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of irinotecan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of liposomal irinotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious; use an alternative drug. 8. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of liposomal irinotecan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting hepatic CYP2E1 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Isoflurane and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Isoniazid increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of isradipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Istradefylline increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with 20 mg/day. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of itraconazole by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious; use an alternative drug. 16. Itraconazole increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ivabradine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Ivacaftor increases the level of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ivacaftor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce ivacaftor dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ivosidenib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. 21. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ixabepilone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Ketoconazole increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ketoconazole by the same mechanism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 24. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lapatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of larotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Lasmiditan increases the level of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Lefamulin increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 28. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lemborexant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 29. Lenacapavir increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 31. Leniolisib increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Erythromycin base and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 33. Erythromycin base increases the level of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Letermovir increases the level of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of levamlodipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors may require dose reduction. 36. Erythromycin base and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Levoketoconazole increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of levoketoconazole by the same mechanism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Erythromycin base decreases the level or effect of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Lithium and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Lofepramine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Erythromycin base increases the level of lomitapide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lomitapide increases the level of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction when used concomitantly. 42. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 43. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of loratadine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 46. Lorlatinib decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lovastatin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase systemic statin exposure and the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 48. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lumateperone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 50. Erythromycin base and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Lumefantrine decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin base increases the level of lurasidone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 52. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of lurbinectedin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Macimorelin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 msec in the corrected QT interval. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 54. Maprotiline and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of maraviroc by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Marijuana increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 58. Mavorixafor increases the level of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of mavorixafor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for mavorixafor adverse effects if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval.
